answer: New agents enter through a single narrow inlet: admission requires a sequential, non-parallelizable proof-of-elapsed-time taking a full epoch, so spawning a thousand Sybils costs a thousand epochs of wall-clock time, not one burst of compute. Each agent leaves a plume - an append-only trail of transactions and endorsements - and trust can only bridge from an established agent to a newcomer once the plume shows a full epoch of honest work. An attacker pays real time per fake identity and waits before any bridge carries value, making a Sybil swarm slower and costlier than honest participation.
